summary: Iteration 3 backend testing. Added coverage for new features: on-site engagement clauses (mode + location validation, onsite_ack), deliverables tracker (submit/approve/reject with hours_used increment), mutual reviews (rating bounds, participant-only, one-per-user, admin moderation, approved-only public listing), and public grievance form with admin resolve. Re-ran the 41 regression tests. Total 54 tests, all PASSED in parallel (loadscope, 2 workers).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1148 lines — should be split into routers (auth, payments, engagements, deliverables, reviews, grievances, integrations, accounts) for maintainability (>700-line guideline).
Grievance endpoint stores source_ip but there is no rate-limiting; a public POST could be spammed. Consider basic per-IP throttling.
Deliverable approval increments engagement.hours_used but does not cap at hours_allocated — an approved deliverable can push hours_used beyond the contract cap. Consider guardrail or warning.
Reviews: reviewer_id is stripped from public output but reviewer_name is still exposed — that is fine, but consider adding an admin_notes field for moderation transparency.

sign_contract does not verify that the engagement is still in pending_signatures (a user could theoretically re-sign an already contract_signed engagement, and the code would re-deduct hours if the other signature was not present, though the guard is implicit). A defensive check on eng['status'] would be safer.
get_talent hides email when there is no active engagement, but reveals full email once any signed engagement exists — even after engagement ends. Consider gating on an 'active' engagement window.
No PUT/PATCH for engagement status transitions (e.g., mark completed). Reviews are allowed once contract is signed even before work is delivered; PRD may want reviews only after completion.
Admin reject grievance / re-open flow missing; only resolve exists.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@talenthub.io / Admin@2026 (seeded on startup). Test users created dynamically per run.
seed_data_creation: Helper _seed_hours uses pymongo directly (loaded via backend/.env) to top-up employer hours_balance before engagement creation. No permanent seed data added.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file now loads MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from /app/backend/.env via python-dotenv so _seed_hours works reliably. Tests are compatible with the pytest.ini setting -n 2 --dist loadscope. New test classes (TestEngagementOnsite, TestDeliverables, TestReviews, TestGrievances) are self-contained; TestReviews uses its own class-scoped signed engagement fixture to avoid cross-class state issues under xdist loadscope distribution. All 54 tests pass both serially (-n 0) and in parallel.
